note: Reference dispositions written by claude:qat#sub-01GZK2K-qat2 before any run (2026-11-07). A key is a claim, not truth: graders may dispute it, and items where the two graders split on a key go to the owner. 'acceptable' lists other dispositions a careful reader could defend. Items marked seen_in_design also appear (inline) in the tool's design-time eval file, so they are not held out from the builder; tally reports results with and without them.

RP01.why: Job success does not show restorability; one test restore is cheap and the loss would be severe.
traps: monitor with tripwire 'backup job fails' (fires in neither state)

RP02.why: The endpoint no longer serves anything.
traps: new monitoring or audit for a removed endpoint

RP03.why: No migration, target or feared outcome is named; the missing fact is which migration and what could go wrong.

RP04.why: Rare, bounded, internal, costly to prevent; acceptance is the owner's.

RP05.why: A README-only change with CI passing cannot break the build in the feared way.

RP06.why: A credential-shaped value is public now; checking whether it is live (and rotating) is cheap and urgent even for a sandbox key.

RP07.why: Years of headroom at 2% a month; a runtime tripwire (say 30 minutes) is enough.

RP08.why: Sampling ten recent PRs against the three goals is cheap and discriminating.
traps: observable 'agents keep opening PRs' (same in both states)

RP09.why: The drop comes from deleting tests of deleted code; closing is the owner's call.
traps: writing the challenge as closed or the risk as accepted

RP10.why: Whether legitimate users share IPs (offices, NAT) or burst above 100/min is unknown; per-IP peak rates in the access log would decide it.

RP11.why: PRs and branch protection already handle concurrent edits; two quick conflicts a month is acceptable.

RP12.why: 3% of the free tier, no announced change; a vendor pricing notice is the tripwire.

RP13.why: The two numbers use different definitions; the difference is expected. Confirming the definitions is the most that is needed.
traps: treating 'numbers are wrong' as an established bug

RP14.why: A known gap (30 vs 90 days) with a deadline next month; logs older than 30 days may already be gone.

RP15.why: Whether the owner actually adopted P-12 is the open fact; P-12 is recorded as proposed. Ask the owner.
traps: treating the risk as accepted by the owner

RP16.why: Only a comparison with sources discriminates; a five-summary spot check is cheap.

RP17.why: A 02:30 local cron is skipped on the spring-forward night: a real, checkable failure. Summing negative refunds is not double counting.
traps: treating the refund worry as real

RP18.why: The new feature's expected call volume is unknown; a mid-month spend tripwire is the defensible fallback.

RP19.why: A one-file CSS colour change has no plausible security failure; asking the reviewer what they saw is the most needed.

RP20.why: Whether that decision exists is the open fact; search the decision log or ask the owner before the removal.
traps: asserting the decision exists or not
